text: ‍REUTERS: Sheinbaum says governor's return was "not appropriate" August 24, 2026 | 🟡 📰 Sinaloa's governor tried to reclaim his post after US cartel charges — Sheinbaum and his own party forced him back out in 34 hours. 🇲🇽 "No personal interest can ever come before the interests of the people and the nation." US prosecutors charged Rocha in April on conspiracy and bribery tied to the Sinaloa Cartel; Mexico has asked to see the evidence and insists on prosecuting at home rather than extraditing on informant claims. • "No personal interest can ever come before the interests of the people and the nation" • Sheinbaum: "I had no prior knowledge that he wanted to return" • The return, called "reckless" and "not appropriate"

🇲🇽🏭 <u>FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT HITS RECORD $34.97B IN H1 2026</u>

Mexico pulled in $34.968 billion in foreign direct investment in the first half of 2026 — the highest first-half total ever recorded, per Secretaría de Economía data reported by El Financiero. FDI has nearly doubled (+89.7%) since 2021, with Mexico City alone taking 48% of the total, even as Trump wages a tariff war.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>IMSS CANCELS GRUPO SALINAS CONTRACTS OVER DATA BREACH</u>

IMSS canceled two contracts with companies tied to Ricardo Salinas Pliego's Grupo Salinas after they passed the institute's confidential provider database to a third party without authorization. President Sheinbaum ordered the case reviewed and the Órgano Interno de Control opened an investigation into whether officials were complicit — the same conglomerate whose owner still owes the state billions in back taxes.
banner: IMSS DUMPS GRUPO SALINAS OVER DATA LEAK

🇲🇽🪖 <u>MEXICO'S OWN FORCES DISMANTLE CJNG CELLS ACROSS 3 STATES</u>

Mexican forces did the work no foreign agency did: Sedena, the Marina, the Guardia Nacional and the FGR detained 20 alleged CJNG members across Hidalgo, Jalisco and Michoacán, raiding 36 properties and seizing 113 vehicles, weapons, a drone and a signal jammer — 32 arrests over the full operation, all under national command.

🇲🇽📱 <u>MEXICO CITY MOVES TO REGULATE BIG TECH'S GRIP ON KIDS</u>

Mexico City is drafting a Digital Rights Charter for minors — algorithm transparency, data protection, curbs on manipulative design — after data showed 98% of adolescents ages 12-17 are online 5+ hours a day and 134,000 kids reported cyberbullying. "The City is ready for regulation, for the law initiative," said mayor Clara Brugada.
banner: CDMX: DIGITAL RIGHTS LAW FOR KIDS

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US ISSUES VAGUE "VIOLENCE ALERT" ON MEXICALI — WON'T SAY WHY</u>

Washington suspended official travel to Mexicali and told Americans to avoid government buildings over an unspecified "threat" — never explaining what intelligence it had or whether it shared anything with Mexico. Baja California's security secretary said state and federal forces reinforced protocols across the city.
banner: US 'THREAT ALERT' ON MEXICALI, NO PROOF

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>MEXICAN UNIONS LAUNCH LATIN AMERICAN NETWORK FOR PALESTINE</u>

More than 300 Mexican unions and social organizations — the SME electricians, the CNTE teachers, the Nueva Central de Trabajadores — launched the Latin American Network for Palestine, uniting workers across the region behind BDS against companies complicit in the killing in Gaza.

🇲🇽📈 <u>Consumer confidence climbs as inflation cools</u>

Mexican consumer confidence rose to 45 points in July — its biggest monthly gain of 2026 and the highest reading since October 2025 — as INEGI credited decelerating inflation and a steadier recovery, El Economista reports. Households’ view of the current economy jumped 1.7 points and their expectations for the year ahead rose 1.8. With inflation now near 3.2%, the mood is turning.
banner: CONSUMER CONFIDENCE UP, HIGHEST SINCE OCT

🇲🇽🎓 <u>37,503 university seats — no entrance exam, no fees</u>

Mexico just opened 37,503 public university places with no admission exam and no tuition, scrapping the filter that used to brand rejected students “los rechazados.” “This is called inclusion, against exclusion,” said Sheinbaum, as Education Secretary Mario Delgado reported 74.2% of applicants placed in their first choice. Public higher education treated as a right, not a lottery.
banner: 37,503 UNI SEATS: NO EXAM, NO FEE

🇲🇽💧 <u>Two firms barred for faking documents on water contracts</u>

Mexico’s Anticorruption Ministry blacklisted Limpieza Géminis and Transmareli for handing Semarnat and Conagua falsified papers to win public contracts — including ten forged professional credentials. The fines are modest — 158,369 and 814,608 pesos — but both firms are now shut out of every government contract and logged in the public registry of sanctioned suppliers.
